title: The Fourier weight shift
statement:
Let $M$ be nonzero, irreducible, Fourier-generic and pure
of weight $w$. Then its Fourier partner $M'$ ([sk-p-dl-a1-middle]) is
pure of weight exactly $w+1$.

proof.text:
Let $v$ be the weight of $M'$ given by [sk-p-dl-a1-some-weight]. Since
shifts do not change the squared absolute values of traces
([sk-def-wrp-l2-definition]), Plancherel ([sk-cor-plancherel]) and
[sk-lem-wft-l2-middle], applied to $M'$ and to $M$, give

$$
 v=\nu(j'_*M')
  =\nu(\operatorname{FT}_\psi((j_*M)[1]))
  =\nu((j_*M)[1])+1=w+1.
$$

Here the outer equalities $
u(j'_*M')=
u(M')=v$ and
$
u(j_*M)=
u(M)=w$ combine [sk-lem-wft-l2-middle] with the dictionary
[sk-thm-wrp-l2-dictionary] between the growth parameter and pure
weights.
